story.title: DeeSy short stories 1: On a demonetized day...
paragraphs_en: As he approached the bank, he took out the notes of Rs. 1000 from his pocket, counted them and stuffed them in. Worried about his knee pain, he joined the long queue. Just then he saw a young man approaching him with a folding chair. “Many of the retired employees of our bank have come to help us with the demonetization work. We thought we would also do our bit to help the elderly”, he said. Sitting on the chair, he noticed the lady ahead of him in the queue struggling to hold her sleeping baby and his toys. He offered to hold the toys. After handing over the toys, she took out a banana and offered it to the small child holding hand of a man standing in ahead of her in the queue. While the child was happily eating the banana, his father had lent his power bank to a youngster ahead of him.

As the battery of his discharged mobile phone started charging, the youngster explained to the aunty standing in front how to fill the demonetization form. Meanwhile, aunty lent her mobile phone to a young girl in front who was telling her parents that she couldn’t call as her phone had zero balance. After her call, she got to know that an elderly lady standing ahead of her wanted to go to the restaurant outside to take her medicines with food but feared that she would lose her place in the queue. The girl assured the lady that she would guard her place. The elderly lady nodded gratefully and stepped out. Outside the restaurant, a shabby child was explaining to his younger sister that he had only one note of Rs. 500 –his father’s daily wages. The elderly lady signalled to the restaurant manager that she would pay for the childrens’ food.

The restaurant manager was approached by a tourist whose old notes of Rs. 500 he accepted. When the tourist rang up his home, his mother told him that she was going to the bank she retired from to help her younger colleagues with the demonetization work…

items.text_en: As he approached the bank, he took out the notes of Rs.
1000 from his pocket, counted them and stuffed them in.
Worried about his knee pain, he joined the long queue.
Just then he saw a young man approaching him with a folding chair.
“Many of the retired employees of our bank have come to help us with the demonetization work.
We thought we would also do our bit to help the elderly”, he said.
Sitting on the chair, he noticed the lady ahead of him in the queue struggling to hold her sleeping baby and his toys.
He offered to hold the toys.
After handing over the toys, she took out a banana and offered it to the small child holding hand of a man standing in ahead of her in the queue.
While the child was happily eating the banana, his father had lent his power bank to a youngster ahead of him.
As the battery of his discharged mobile phone started charging, the youngster explained to the aunty standing in front how to fill the demonetization form.
Meanwhile, aunty lent her mobile phone to a young girl in front who was telling her parents that she couldn’t call as her phone had zero balance.

After her call, she got to know that an elderly lady standing ahead of her wanted to go to the restaurant outside to take her medicines with food but feared that she would lose her place in the queue.
The girl assured the lady that she would guard her place.
The elderly lady nodded gratefully and stepped out.
Outside the restaurant, a shabby child was explaining to his younger sister that he had only one note of Rs.
500 –his father’s daily wages.
The elderly lady signalled to the restaurant manager that she would pay for the childrens’ food.
The restaurant manager was approached by a tourist whose old notes of Rs.
500 he accepted.
When the tourist rang up his home, his mother told him that she was going to the bank she retired from to help her younger colleagues with the demonetization work…
